modules.description: One Qdrant collection alias: the name clients use, pointed at the collection that should serve them.
modules.name: alias

absent.description:
Remove ONE alias (no qdrant CLI, no shell). The collection it pointed at is
untouched — an alias is a name, and removing it removes nothing else.

Idempotent: an alias that is not there is a no-op that sends no mutating
request and reports changed=false. The list is read first because Qdrant
answers 200 to the deletion of an alias that does not exist, so acting on the
response would report a change on every run. The list is read again
afterwards and a removal that did not take fails the step.
Output.previous carries what it pointed at. No dry-run preview.

addr.description: Qdrant REST API address as host:port (e.g. "qdrant-1:6333"). WITHOUT a scheme — http/https is chosen by `tls`, and a scheme here is refused rather than allowed to contradict it.

api_key.description: Qdrant API key (vault-ref in operator input; keeper resolves it before Apply). Masked in logs/traces/UI (secret). Sent in the `api-key` REQUEST HEADER only — never in the URL (Qdrant answers 401 to a key in the query string, so no URL form of it exists to leak) and never in a command argument, since nothing here spawns a process for `ps` to read.

timeout_sec.description: Per-request timeout in seconds. Bounds every call, so a wedged instance fails the task instead of hanging the run. Raise it for a create over many shards.

tls.description: Speak https to the API. Default false (plaintext http). A non-boolean value is REFUSED rather than coerced: the coercion would fall back on the side that sends the api-key in the clear.

tls_ca.description: PEM CA certificate used to verify the server certificate (RootCAs). Masked (secret). Resolved keeper-side from Vault in the render phase.

tls_cert.description: PEM client certificate for mTLS (optional, only together with tls_key). Masked (secret).

tls_key.description: PEM client key for mTLS (optional, only together with tls_cert). Masked (secret); does not end up in events or errors.

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of server certificate verification. Default false (verification on — default secure).

present.description:
Point ONE alias at ONE collection over Qdrant's REST API (no qdrant CLI,
no shell). Creates the alias when it does not exist and RE-POINTS it when it
points somewhere else — re-pointing is the blue-green swap this object exists
for, it costs no data, and Qdrant applies the change atomically, so clients
never see the alias resolve to nothing.

The target collection is checked first: an alias to a collection that does
not exist fails with both names in the message, rather than with Qdrant's own
error, which names only the alias.

Idempotent: an alias already pointing at the declared collection is a no-op
that sends no mutating request and reports changed=false. `changed` comes
from reading the alias list before and after, NEVER from the response —
Qdrant answers 200 to a create that re-points and to one that changes
nothing, so the response cannot tell the two apart. Output.previous carries
what the alias used to point at, which is what a rollback step needs.
No dry-run preview.

Sent in the `api-key` REQUEST HEADER only — never in the URL (Qdrant answers 401 to a key in the query string, so no URL form of it exists to leak) and never in a command argument, since nothing here spawns a process for `ps` to read.

collection.description: The collection the alias must resolve to. Must already exist.

name.description: The alias — the name clients connect to. A URL-unsafe value is refused.

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of server certificate verification. Default false (verification on — default secure).

modules.description: One Qdrant collection: probed, declared with its vector and sharding parameters, or removed.
modules.name: collection

absent.description:
Remove ONE collection and everything in it (no qdrant CLI, no shell).

Idempotent: a collection that is not there is a no-op that sends no DELETE
(changed=false). It does READ first — Qdrant answers 200 {"result":false}
to a delete that removed nothing, and this state reports what actually
happened rather than what was asked. The removal is verified by reading the
collection back.

This destroys the collection's contents. Unlike recreated it carries no
confirm_destroy, because `absent` IS the declaration — there is no reading of
it under which the data survives. No dry-run preview.

present.description:
Declare ONE collection and reconcile what CAN be reconciled (no qdrant CLI,
no shell). Creates it when missing.

★ Qdrant divides a collection's settings in two, and this state respects the
line rather than pretending it is not there. `replication_factor`,
`write_consistency_factor`, `on_disk_payload`, `hnsw_config`,
`optimizers_config`, `quantization_config` and the per-vector `hnsw_config`/
`quantization_config`/`on_disk`/`memory` are reconciled in place. A vector's
`size` and `distance`, plus `shard_number`, `sharding_method` and
`wal_config`, exist ONLY at creation time.

If a live collection differs in one of those, this state FAILS and names the
field, its live value and the declared one. It does not quietly recreate the
collection — that would destroy every point in it — and it does not quietly
send the update either, because Qdrant ACCEPTS an update to those fields,
answers 200 {"result":true} and discards it. Reporting that as a change
would be a lie that repeats on every run. To rebuild deliberately, use
qdrant.collection.recreated.

Idempotent: a collection already in the declared shape sends no request at
all and reports changed=false. `changed` is decided by comparing the
collection before and after, never from the response — Qdrant's response
does not distinguish an update it applied from one it threw away. Every
write is read back and verified for the same reason.

Only DECLARED keys are compared, so a partial declaration converges; the
cost is that this state cannot reset a setting back to Qdrant's default.
Points, aliases and payload indexes are not its subject — see qdrant.alias
and qdrant.index. No dry-run preview.

Sent in the `api-key` REQUEST HEADER only — never in the URL (Qdrant answers 401 to a key in the query string, so no URL form of it exists to leak) and never in a command argument, since nothing here spawns a process for `ps` to read.

Only the keys you declare are compared — Qdrant reports this map fully populated with its defaults, so comparing the whole thing would report drift on every run.

name.description: Collection name. Addresses a URL path segment, so it carries no whitespace, slash, "?" or "#".

on_disk_payload.description: Keep payloads on disk rather than in RAM. Reconciled on a live collection.

optimizers_config.description: Optimizer settings (deleted_threshold, vacuum_min_vector_number, default_segment_number, max_segment_size, memmap_threshold, indexing_threshold, flush_interval_sec, max_optimization_threads). Reconciled on a live collection. Note Qdrant WRITES this as `optimizers_config` and READS it back as `optimizer_config`; the module handles the two spellings. Only declared keys are compared.

quantization_config.description: Quantization settings (scalar / product / binary). Reconciled on a live collection. Only declared keys are compared.

sharding_method.description: "auto" (default) or "custom" (shard keys). CREATION-ONLY. Qdrant omits this from a collection left on "auto", which this module treats as "auto" rather than as drift.

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of server certificate verification. Default false (verification on — default secure).

write_consistency_factor.description: Replicas that must acknowledge a write. Reconciled on a live collection.

probed.description:
Read a collection's state over the REST API (no qdrant CLI, no shell).
Read-only, changed=false by design.

Output.exists says whether it is there at all — an ABSENT collection is a
reading, not a failure, because "create it only if missing" is a gate a
scenario has to be able to write. Output.status is Qdrant's own
green/yellow/grey/red, which is what to wait on after a restart or an index
change; Output.optimizer_status, .points_count, .segments_count and
.indexed_vectors_count come along for diagnostics. No dry-run preview.

recreated.description:
As qdrant.collection.present, but authorized to DROP AND REBUILD the
collection when the declared shape cannot be reached on the live one
(a changed vector `size` or `distance`, `shard_number`, `sharding_method`,
`wal_config`, or a named vector that exists and is no longer declared).
Requires confirm_destroy: true.

★ WHEN IT FIRES, EVERY POINT IN THE COLLECTION IS LOST. Qdrant has no
in-place path for these settings and no rename, so there is nothing to
preserve behind. Take a snapshot first (qdrant.snapshot.created) if the
contents matter.

It is NOT "recreate every run": a collection that already matches is left
untouched with changed=false, and one that differs only in reconcilable
settings is patched in place exactly as `present` would. Recreating
unconditionally would destroy the data on every run, which is the opposite
of what a declared state means. No dry-run preview.

modules.description: One payload field index of a Qdrant collection: the index that makes a filter on that field fast.
modules.name: index

absent.description:
Remove ONE payload field index (no qdrant CLI, no shell). The field and its
values are untouched — only the index over them goes, so filters on it get
slower and nothing is lost.

Idempotent: a field that is not indexed is a no-op that sends no request and
reports changed=false. Qdrant answers 200 to the deletion of an index that
does not exist, so the response is not the source of `changed` here either:
the payload_schema is read before and after. Output.previous carries the type
the index had. No dry-run preview.

Sent in the `api-key` REQUEST HEADER only — never in the URL (Qdrant answers 401 to a key in the query string, so no URL form of it exists to leak) and never in a command argument, since nothing here spawns a process for `ps` to read.

tls_skip_verify.description: EXPLICIT opt-out of server certificate verification. Default false (verification on — default secure).

present.description:
Ensure ONE payload field of a collection is indexed as the declared type
(no qdrant CLI, no shell). Built with wait=true, so the step returns when the
index is actually built rather than when the request was accepted.

A field already indexed under a DIFFERENT type is dropped and built again,
in place and without asking. That is deliberate and it is the difference
between this object and qdrant.collection: rebuilding a payload index
destroys an INDEX, not data — the points and their payloads are untouched
and Qdrant reads them again. What it does cost is a WINDOW: between the drop
and the rebuild, filters on that field fall back to a full scan, which on a
large collection is slow rather than wrong. Schedule it accordingly.

Idempotent: a field already indexed as the declared type is a no-op that
sends no request and reports changed=false. The result is read back from the
collection's payload_schema and an index that did not appear fails the step.
Output.previous carries the type it had before. No dry-run preview.

addr.description: Qdrant REST API address as host:port (e.g. "qdrant-1:6333"). WITHOUT a scheme — http/https is chosen by `tls`, and a scheme here is refused rather than allowed to contradict it.

api_key.description: Qdrant API key (vault-ref in operator input; keeper resolves it before Apply). Masked in logs/traces/UI (secret). Sent in the `api-key` REQUEST HEADER only — never in the URL (Qdrant answers 401 to a key in the query string, so no URL form of it exists to leak) and never in a command argument, since nothing here spawns a process for `ps` to read.

collection.description: Collection holding the field. Must already exist — this state does not create one.

field.description: Payload field name. Addresses a URL path segment, so it carries no whitespace, slash, "?" or "#".

schema.description: Field type to index as. Only the plain string schemas are managed here, because they are the ones Qdrant echoes back verbatim as `data_type` and can therefore be compared exactly. Qdrant's OBJECT schema form (a text index with a tokenizer, a parameterised integer index) is NOT supported: the read-back reports only the data type, so this module could not tell one tokenizer from another and would report converged on an index that is not. A half-compared index is worse than an unsupported one.

modules.description: A live Qdrant server: liveness, readiness and version probes.
modules.name: instance

pinged.description:
Liveness-probe Qdrant with GET /healthz (no qdrant CLI, no shell).
Read-only, changed=false by design — a probe, not a mutation.
Output.result carries the server's own line ("healthz check passed"), so
register.self.result works in a health gate (retry/until/failed_when) the
same way it does on the redis artifact.

/healthz is served WITHOUT authentication even on an instance that has an
api-key configured, so this state reaches a Qdrant whose credential the
scenario does not hold. A non-2xx answer FAILS the step: the question is
"is it answering at all", and a no is worth stopping on. No dry-run preview.

ready-probed.description:
Readiness-probe Qdrant with GET /readyz (no qdrant CLI, no shell).
Read-only, changed=false by design. Ready means every shard is loaded and
the instance can serve queries — which is what a rolling restart must wait
on, because /healthz answers long before that point.

A not-ready answer is a READING, not a failure: Output.ready is false and
the step succeeds, so `until: register.self.ready` can wait it out. Failing
instead would end the run before the gate ever looked. An UNREACHABLE
instance does fail, and the distinction is load-bearing: a gate that reads
"host is gone" as "still starting" burns its whole retry budget on an
instance that is never coming back. No dry-run preview.

version-probed.description:
Version-probe Qdrant with GET / (no qdrant CLI, no shell). Read-only,
changed=false by design. Output.version is the plain version string
("1.18.3"), Output.commit the build commit, Output.title the server banner.

Use it to gate a step on a feature the running Qdrant may not have. An
answer with no version field FAILS rather than reporting an empty string:
something is answering on that address, but it is not this API. No dry-run
preview.

addr.description: Qdrant REST API address as host:port (e.g. "qdrant-1:6333"). WITHOUT a scheme — http/https is chosen by `tls`, and a scheme here is refused rather than allowed to contradict it.

api_key.description: Qdrant API key (vault-ref in operator input; keeper resolves it before Apply). Masked in logs/traces/UI (secret). Sent in the `api-key` REQUEST HEADER only — never in the URL (Qdrant answers 401 to a key in the query string, so no URL form of it exists to leak) and never in a command argument, since nothing here spawns a process for `ps` to read.

timeout_sec.description: Per-request timeout in seconds. Bounds every call, so a wedged instance fails the task instead of hanging the run. Raise it for a create over many shards.

modules.description: A snapshot of one Qdrant collection: taken, or removed by name.
modules.name: snapshot

absent.description:
Remove ONE snapshot of a collection by name (no qdrant CLI, no shell).

Idempotent: a snapshot that is not there is a no-op that sends no DELETE
(changed=false). It does LIST first, and that is not only for the changed
flag — Qdrant answers 404 to a delete of a snapshot it does not have, so a
blind DELETE would fail the second run of the very same step.

A collection that does not exist also reads as absent rather than failing: a
cleanup step that runs after the collection is gone has got what it asked
for. The removal is verified by listing afterwards. No dry-run preview.

created.description:
Take a snapshot of ONE collection over the REST API (no qdrant CLI, no
shell). Output.name is the snapshot's name, which is the only handle on it
and which QDRANT chooses — it is built from a timestamp and cannot be set.

★ Read this before relying on it as a state. Taking a snapshot is an
OPERATION: with max_age_sec omitted, every run takes another one and reports
changed=true, because nothing in the Qdrant API expresses "make sure a
backup exists".

max_age_sec is what makes it declarable: with it the state reads "a snapshot
of this collection younger than N seconds exists", and a run inside that
window sends nothing and reports changed=false. Use it whenever the step is
in a scenario that runs more than once.

A collection that does not exist FAILS rather than passing quietly — a
backup step that succeeds on a missing collection is worse than one that
stops. The snapshot is verified by listing the collection's snapshots
afterwards. No dry-run preview.

addr.description: Qdrant REST API address as host:port (e.g. "qdrant-1:6333"). WITHOUT a scheme — http/https is chosen by `tls`, and a scheme here is refused rather than allowed to contradict it.

api_key.description: Qdrant API key (vault-ref in operator input; keeper resolves it before Apply). Masked in logs/traces/UI (secret). Sent in the `api-key` REQUEST HEADER only — never in the URL (Qdrant answers 401 to a key in the query string, so no URL form of it exists to leak) and never in a command argument, since nothing here spawns a process for `ps` to read.

collection.description: Collection to snapshot. Addresses a URL path segment, so it carries no whitespace, slash, "?" or "#".

max_age_sec.description: Take a snapshot only if the newest existing one is OLDER than this many seconds; otherwise do nothing and report changed=false. Omitted or 0 means always take one, which makes this step an operation rather than a state. The comparison uses Qdrant's own creation_time, which is UTC.
